verdict: Lilly's revenue jumped 56% to $19.8B as Mounjaro sales more than doubled to $8.7B — and it kept $7.4B as profit, nearly triple a year ago.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes and weight-loss shot (tirzepatide). U.S. sales were $4.2B; sales outside the U.S. more than tripled to $4.4B after Mounjaro joined China's reimbursement list.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The same drug sold for obesity in the U.S., Canada and Japan — U.S. sales rose 79% to $4.1B on strong demand, partly offset by lower prices.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else — cancer, immunology and diabetes medicines, including a one-time $250M Jardiance benefit from partner Boehringer Ingelheim.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Finding and testing new medicines — 18% of revenue.

opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams and launch campaigns for new medicines.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought with acquisitions, expensed immediately — $0.52 of EPS this quarter.

otherDetail: Net other expense of $65M — interest costs of $253M, partly covered by $188M of other income.
footerNote: Reported (GAAP) figures throughout; Lilly's non-GAAP net income was $7,663M (EPS $8.55).
follow100Note: Two shots — Mounjaro and Zepbound — brought in $64.76 of every $100. Even after $2.95 of one-off acquired-research charges in every $100, Lilly kept $37.35 as profit.

takeaways.title: Mounjaro more than doubled
takeaways.text: Mounjaro revenue rose 125% to $8.7B. Growth came from volume — more prescriptions — even as prices fell, including after Mounjaro joined China's National Reimbursed Drug List.

takeaways.title: Smaller one-off charges
takeaways.text: Acquired IPR&D charges fell to $584M ($0.52 of EPS) from $1,572M a year ago — one reason reported profit nearly tripled. Asset impairment and restructuring added $279M.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised
takeaways.text: Lilly raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $82–85B and won FDA approval for Foundayo, its GLP-1 pill for weight loss — the next product in the franchise.

oneTimers: Acquired IPR&D of $584M — research bought via acquisitions and expensed immediately. It cost $0.52 of EPS; a year ago the same line was $1,572M ($1.72 of EPS).
Asset impairment, restructuring and other special charges of $279M, versus $35M a year ago.
Jardiance revenue outside the U.S. included a one-time $250M benefit tied to the Boehringer Ingelheim collaboration; a year ago the same benefit was $370M.
